title: How deep a temperature cycle reaches into soil
caption: The amplitude of a periodic surface temperature falls as e^{−z/δ} with δ = √(2α/ω). For soil (α = 5 × 10⁻⁷ m² s⁻¹) the daily cycle (ω = 7.3 × 10⁻⁵ s⁻¹) has δ = 0.12 m, so it has all but vanished by half a metre. A cycle 365 times longer has δ larger by √365 ≈ 19: 2.2 m (the lesson's ≈ 2.3 m uses the rounded 0.12 m).
alt: Graph of relative temperature amplitude against depth in metres: a daily curve falling to 1/e at 0.12 m and an annual curve falling to 1/e at 2.2 m.
description: The horizontal axis is depth below the surface in metres; the vertical axis is the temperature swing as a fraction of the surface swing.
Daily cycle: e^{−z/0.12}, falling to 1/e (0.37) at z = δ = 0.12 m.
Annual cycle: δ = 0.12 × √365 = 2.2 m, 19 times deeper.
